component.name: Pelican
component.summary: Put your own music on a Garmin watch

description.p: Pelican moves your own music files onto a Garmin watch over a USB cable. Choose the music, and it tags, converts every file to one known-good MP3 profile, sends it, and reads each file back to prove it arrived intact. It needs no Garmin Express, no cloud service and no vendor account.
Pelican makes no network connections. Your music stays on your computer, and your fitness data stays on your watch.

ul.li: FLAC, WAV, ALAC, AAC, MP3, OGG, Opus, AIFF, WMA and more are converted to one profile: MP3, 192 kbps CBR, 44.1 kHz stereo, ID3v2.3
Tags missing from a file are filled from its folder and file name
Every file is sent under a name never used on that watch before, then read back and hashed
A per-device ledger of every name sent, kept across runs
Backs up the watch's own files before a factory reset, and starts a fresh ledger after one
A command-line tool, pelican, for scripts and terminals

description.p: The watch has to be reachable by your user account. Pelican shows the one-line command that installs its USB rule on the host the first time it cannot open the watch.

screenshot.caption: The connected watch, with free space and room for tracks
Sending, with every file read back and verified
Backing up the watch before a factory reset

description.p: Pelican rebuilt for Linux: a desktop app alongside the command-line tool, and every file sent is read back and verified.
